assertions.name: C1_tau_reproduces_the_DG_WORKED_figure_eight_value
assertions.source: |tau(4_1)| = sqrt(3)/2 to 0.0. This validates the implementation being consumed — the module records that THREE 1-loop implementations existed in this repo and disagreed, so consuming one without this check would be unsafe

assertions.name: C3_the_retriangulator_REALLY_perturbs_the_triangulation
assertions.source: every knot shows >1 distinct polarization datum, so the invariance test below is not vacuous — an invariance check passes trivially when nothing was varied

assertions.name: the_RAW_POLARIZATION_datum_is_NOT_a_manifold_invariant
assertions.source: one manifold, 30 retriangulations: 6_2 gives 9 distinct values, 5_2 4, 4_1 3. The node count IS a manifold invariant, so a construction reading the matrix entries directly cannot equal it without a separate triangulation-invariance argument

assertions.name: C2_tau_IS_triangulation_invariant
assertions.source: spread < 1e-30 over retriangulations of 4_1 and 6_2, while C3 confirms the triangulation genuinely changed. So triangulation-invariant functionals of the NZ datum EXIST

assertions.name: tau_SEPARATES_all_five_knots_the_SNF_could_not
assertions.source: all 10 pairwise gaps exceed 1e-30; the smallest is 0.555151. The SNF gave these five knots ONE value; a triangulation-invariant functional of the same datum gives five

assertions.name: CORRECTION_there_are_SIX_usable_points_not_TWO
assertions.source: an earlier version of this probe claimed the corpus could not TEST a tau->C map — certified C for three knots, tau undefined on the non-hyperbolic 3_1, so two points. THAT WAS WRONG and the error was mine: the fixtures were never enumerated. The ptolemy DB is firewalled (re-verified, 403 on CONNECT), but the wheel ships sl2 fixtures for 7 manifolds and 6 are 1-cusped hyperbolic with both a defined tau and a certified irreducible count: ['4_1', '5_2', 'm135', 's000', 't00000', 'v0000']. Six points against a two-parameter family leaves four degrees of freedom, so a candidate IS testable. The blocker was overstated 3x

assertions.name: the_irreducible_count_is_NOT_the_tetrahedron_count
assertions.source: irreducible = N holds for 4 of 6 and FAILS for ['m135', 'v0000']. Worth stating because it is the first thing one would wrongly assume from the 4_1/5_2 pair alone, where both happen to coincide

assertions.name: but_STILL_no_tau_to_C_map_is_proposed
assertions.source: six points make a candidate testable; they do not make fishing for one legitimate. Searching a functional form across six points and reporting the winner is the numerology this repo forbids. A map is separate work that must state its hypothesis BEFORE looking, and the census manifolds are valid for testing whether a relation exists while NOT automatically valid as D1-b nodes — D1-b's setup is about knots in S^3, and four of the six are not

assertions.name: CONSEQUENCE_the_dictionary_is_LOCATED_not_excluded
assertions.source: it must be strictly finer than the Smith normal form (part 1) and triangulation-invariant (this part). That class is non-empty — tau is in it — so D1-b is narrowed to a well-posed search, not refuted. What is missing to PROSECUTE it is NOT data: the correction above found six offline points, enough to test a candidate. What is missing is a HYPOTHESIS stated before looking. More certified counts (ptolemy DB, firewalled; or magma) would strengthen a test but are no longer the blocker I reported them to be

description: D1-b (qou-q9ih) part 2, closing the side part 1 left open. Part 1: the SNF of the NZ gluing matrix is a function of N alone, so the dictionary must be polarization-dependent. Here: the raw polarization-dependent datum is NOT a manifold invariant -- 30 retriangulations of 6_2 give ~a dozen distinct values of (N, SNF(P), det P, rank P) for P = A_edge.B_edge^T -- the exact count is STOCHASTIC, randomize() walks a random move sequence and successive runs gave 9 and 11, so read this run's figures from polarization_variance_under_retriangulation rather than quoting one; the assertion tests only that it moves. Together a pincer: the basis-independent invariant is too coarse, the raw polarization datum too fine, and the node count is a manifold invariant. CONSTRUCTIVE half: the class of triangulation-invariant NZ functionals is non-empty and the corpus holds a verified member -- the Dimofte-Garoufalidis 1-loop invariant tau (one_loop_torsion.py), measured here as triangulation-invariant to 1e-30 and separating all five N=5 knots the SNF collided. So D1-b's dictionary is LOCATED, not excluded. NO tau->C map is proposed. CORRECTION carried in this witness: an earlier version claimed the corpus could not TEST such a map, on the ground that certified C exists for only three knots and tau is undefined on the non-hyperbolic 3_1, leaving two points. That was wrong -- the fixtures were never enumerated. The ptolemy DB is indeed firewalled (re-verified 403 on CONNECT), but the snappy wheel ships sl2 fixtures for SEVEN manifolds, SIX of them 1-cusped hyperbolic with both a defined tau and a certified irreducible count (4_1, 5_2, m135, s000, t00000, v0000). So a candidate IS testable, six points against a two-parameter family; the blocker was overstated 3x. Caveats recorded: four are census manifolds not knots in S^3, the abelian convention does not carry over so the common currency is the irreducible count, and irreducible = N fails for m135 and v0000. Also a trap: one_loop does NOT guard against non-hyperbolic input -- it returns 0.5 for 3_1 without raising, so a returned value is not evidence of hyperbolicity. mpmath at 40 dps throughout; no float64. Scope-(a); nothing wired; no fit.

fixture_manifolds_skipped.3_1: not hyperbolic (contains flat tetrahedra); tau is undefined, though one_loop returns a value without raising

ptolemy_db_reachability.verified_by: curl to ptolemy.unhyperbolic.org AND snappy's own retrieve_solutions() for 6_1
ptolemy_db_reachability.consequence: the bundled wheel fixtures are the whole offline certified-count dataset; they were never enumerated before, which is how the 'two points' claim arose

scope.shows: the raw polarization-dependent NZ datum is not a manifold invariant; together with part 1's SNF degeneracy this brackets the dictionary between too-coarse and too-fine
scope.constructive: the bracketed class is non-empty; the DG 1-loop tau is triangulation-invariant and separates the five N=5 knots the SNF collided
scope.does_NOT_show: that tau, or any triangulation-invariant functional, PRODUCES the node count. tau is a complex number, not an integer count; separating is not counting
scope.why_no_map_is_offered: not for lack of data — CORRECTED: six usable (tau, irreducible) points exist offline, so a candidate IS testable. No map is offered because searching a functional form across six points and reporting the winner is a fit; a map must state its hypothesis first
scope.superseded_claim: an earlier version said TWO points and that the corpus could not test any map. Wrong by 3x; the wheel fixtures were never enumerated
scope.what_would_unblock_MORE_points: the ptolemy database (firewalled, 403 re-verified) or magma
scope.trap: one_loop does NOT guard against non-hyperbolic input — it returns 0.5 for 3_1 without raising. A returned value is not evidence of hyperbolicity; check solution_type() yourself
scope.arithmetic: mpmath at 40 dps for tau; exact integers for the polarization datum; no float64, no float() outside mp.nstr rendering
